document_metadata.title: 1、INT. SUV -- DAY
document_metadata.summary: An SUV speeds as Lara attempts to exit, causing John to grab her, leading to a chaotic near-collision. The scene cuts to black with a title: THE LAST THREE YEARS.

entities.name: Lara attempts to exit speeding SUV
entities.description: Lara, the passenger in a moving SUV, unfastens her seat belt and reaches for the door handle, then opens the door while the vehicle is in motion.

entities.name: John dives to grab Lara as SUV door opens
entities.description: John, the driver of the SUV, sees the passenger door open and lunges across the vehicle in an attempt to grab Lara and prevent her from falling or jumping out.

entities.name: SUV loses control and swerves through traffic
entities.description: As a result of the distraction and physical movement inside, the SUV spins out of control, causing horns to blare and tires to screech as nearby cars swerve to avoid a collision.

document_metadata.title: 2、INT. STEAK HOUSE -- NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Tensions erupt during dinner as Erit's provocative remarks about John spark a heated exchange with Lara, revealing underlying relationship conflicts; the men intervene to defuse the confrontation.

entities.name: Erit expresses opinion that women should not work for women
entities.description: During dinner, Erit states her belief that women should never work for other women, claiming they are often threatened, especially if less attractive.

entities.name: Lara confronts Erit about her views on women in the workplace
entities.description: Lara challenges Erit's assertion, arguing that her own boss is difficult because she is a 'bitch,' not because she is a woman.

entities.name: John encourages Erit to continue provocative commentary
entities.description: John egges Erit on by asking leading questions about workplace dynamics, amplifying the tension and humor of the exchange.

entities.name: Mick laughs and compares preferring to work under John rather than Erit
entities.description: In response to the escalating banter, Mick jokes that he'd rather work under his brother John than under Erit, prompting more laughter.

entities.description: Lara places cash on the tray next to Mick's credit card, indicating she is settling her portion of the dinner expenses.

entities.name: John and Mick share laughter over family banter
entities.description: John and his brother Mick repeatedly laugh together during the dinner, bonding over the sarcastic and provocative exchanges between their partners.

entities.description: Lara challenges Erit on her suggestive comment, interpreting it as inappropriate sexual innuendo directed at her husband, further intensifying the conflict.

entities.name: Lara enters the visiting room and greets John and Luke
entities.description: Lara enters the visiting room after being let in by a guard, hurries to John, gives him a real kiss, and attempts to engage with her son Luke, who is playing with Legos.

entities.name: Luke reluctantly gives Lara a kiss
entities.description: After being prompted by Lara and then John, Luke gives Lara a brief peck on the cheek before returning to his Legos without further interaction.

entities.name: Lara asks about Luke's daily life and school experience
entities.description: Lara inquires whether John read her letters to Luke, asks what he built with Legos, and questions how Luke felt on his first day of school, showing concern for her son's well-being.

entities.name: John describes Luke's first day of school and lunch routine
entities.description: John tells Lara that he walked Luke to class, that Luke did not wave back, and that he prepared a turkey sandwich with no vegetables, which Luke claimed he ate along with an apple.

entities.name: John hands Lara a pack of photos of Luke
entities.description: John gives Lara a collection of photographs showing Luke at school, including images of his friends, desk, and teacher, which Lara eagerly looks through.

entities.name: Lara suggests John may need to move school districts
entities.description: Lara observes the photos and advises John that he might have to move to another school district, possibly due to concerns about education or proximity.

entities.name: John informs Lara about contacting a realtor
entities.description: John confirms that he has already spoken to a realtor, indicating he is taking steps toward relocating as suggested.

entities.name: Lara asks about her mother's visit and the appeal status
entities.description: Lara inquires when her mother will visit and presses John for information about the status of her appeal, showing emotional investment in both family and legal matters.

entities.name: John reveals he knows about the appeal but chooses not to tell Lara
entities.description: John confirms he has received information regarding Lara's appeal but decides to withhold the details from her during their visit.

entities.name: Lara expresses concern about the court ruling delay and insists the woman was present during the incident
entities.description: Lara argues with John, emphasizing her belief that the woman involved in the incident was clearly there and could not have simply disappeared, citing physical evidence like a button popping from her purse.

entities.name: John informs Lara that Meyer is hiring a new investigator to reexamine the evidence
entities.description: John tells Lara that a new investigator will be appointed by Meyer to review all the evidence again, offering a potential avenue for progress in the case.

entities.name: Lara sarcastically comments on the financial strain of pursuing the investigation
entities.description: Lara makes a bitter remark about how the legal efforts have not yet fully bankrupted them, highlighting the emotional and financial toll of the ongoing case.

entities.name: Lara affectionately teases John about lying but compliments his appearance
entities.description: In a moment of tenderness, Lara strokes John's face, calls him a liar, and affectionately remarks on his handsomeness, showing emotional intimacy despite the stress.

entities.name: Lara asks John to run for governor to change the prison's conjugal visit policy
entities.description: Lara jokingly yet earnestly requests that John run for governor so he can change the rule prohibiting conjugal visits, expressing her despair over enduring twenty more years without physical closeness.

entities.name: John humorously agrees to run for governor as a favor to Lara
entities.description: Responding to Lara's request, John pretends to consider the absurdity of the task and says he can fulfill that particular favor, blending humor with emotional support.

entities.name: Lara breaks down emotionally and questions if Luke will ever want to kiss her again
entities.description: After a moment of forced optimism, Lara stares at Luke playing and quietly asks John if she will ever regain her son's affection, revealing deep maternal insecurity and grief.

entities.name: John comforts Lara by holding her tightly and stroking her back
entities.description: Seeing Lara's emotional collapse, John embraces her, gently stroking her back to soothe her, offering silent reassurance during her moment of vulnerability.

entities.name: Lara insists she is okay while showing signs of emotional distress
entities.description: Lara repeatedly tells John she is fine even as her demeanor reveals inner turmoil, indicating her attempt to maintain composure despite overwhelming sadness.

entities.name: John reassures Lara that everything will be fine and promises her
entities.description: John tells Lara he knows she is struggling but affirms that things will work out, offering a promise of hope and stability in the face of uncertainty.
